claims.claim: 100-point rubric weights and the 90 bar

Fear appeals work on average (d≈0.29, 127 papers) and work clearly better when paired with an efficacy message (how to act, that it works). Contrary to the popular rule, low-efficacy fear appeals did NOT backfire on average (significant negative effects 9/154 vs 3/94 studies); high fear did no better than moderate fear (d=0.02). Witte1992 predicts avoidance under high threat + low efficacy, but that is a theory proposition.
claims.strength: A (Tannenbaum2015 read via the full dissertation version, same data; Witte1992 abstract only)
claims.craft_notes: Still pair risk with an easy action (it raises effect); use moderate, not extreme, fear; never exaggerate the risk (ethics + FACT_CHECK_WORKFLOW).

claims.claim: Curiosity is an inverted-U of confidence: highest when people feel about 50% sure
claims.craft_notes: hooks that pose a question the viewer half-knows

claims.claim: Facial-expression models differ across cultures; inner emotion cannot be read from a face alone
claims.craft_notes: direct emotion with context + action + voice, never face only

claims.claim: Audio may lag picture slightly but must not lead it (broadcast tolerance about +45 ms lead / -125 ms lag)
claims.craft_notes: SFX/lip-sync: never early; up to ~1 frame late is safe

claims.claim: Narration + identical on-screen text costs very little (redundancy effect small); condensed keywords help
claims.craft_notes: subtitles OK on story clips; extra headline 1-4 keywords

claims.claim: Working memory holds about 4 chunks
claims.craft_notes: derived rule: ~4 meaning units per slide (heuristic, not tested here)

claims.claim: Many popular quotes attributed to Buddha, Lao Tzu, Marcus Aurelius, Seneca, Frankl are misattributed
claims.craft_notes: use only lines from the genuine list; else write it as the character's own words

claims.claim: Colour-psychology effects are small or unreliable: red before a cognitive test has ~no effect after bias correction; red-attractiveness is small (d≈0.13–0.26) and shrinking. Write 'often associated with', never 'makes people…'.
claims.craft_notes: Colour meaning still matters as convention and context; it is just not a reliable causal lever.

claims.claim: Hue-harmony templates (complementary, triadic…) are not a quality rule: across >2 million user palettes people did not gravitate to them and template fit did not predict ratings; lightness contrast and hue similarity mattered more.
claims.craft_notes: Templates stay useful as starting points (CRAFT).

claims.claim: People prefer curved over angular contours on average (meta-analysis g=0.39); the 'angular = danger' link shows mainly in implicit tests; 'square = stable' has no evidence.
claims.strength: strong for curvature preference; weak for specific shape meanings
claims.craft_notes: Use round shapes for warm/safe characters (Mint & Tao); angular for tension — as tendency, not law.

claims.claim: Close camera distance (≈45 cm vs 135 cm) changes face proportions and lowers trust/attractiveness ratings — a camera-distance effect, not a lens effect.
claims.craft_notes: Product/people portraits: step back and use a longer focal length for flattering faces.

claims.claim: Luminance contrast outweighs chroma for pulling the eye: in our controlled grade test darkening the surround raised focal saliency +0.24 vs desaturating +0.05 (one image, model saliency).
claims.craft_notes: Fix order: crop/remove competitor > darken surround > desaturate.

claims.claim: The '8-second / goldfish' attention span figure has no traceable research source.
claims.craft_notes: Never cite attention-span numbers; use our own Insights.

claims.claim: Clickbait headlines did not raise curiosity or clicks over plain headlines in controlled experiments.
claims.craft_notes: Hooks should promise what the clip delivers.

claims.claim: Scheduled 20-second breaks during 40-min tablet reading did not reduce symptoms (small study); 20-20-20 is advice, not proven treatment.
claims.craft_notes: Say 'พักสายตาช่วยให้สบายขึ้นได้' not 'ป้องกัน/รักษา'.

claims.claim: UV-B exposure is associated with cortical cataract in most epidemiologic studies.
claims.craft_notes: Say 'ลดความเสี่ยง', never 'ป้องกันต้อ'.

claims.claim: Generational differences in work attitudes are small to near zero in meta-analysis; avoid generation stereotypes.
claims.craft_notes: Segment by real audience data, not by age labels.
